questions.key_step: Normal parallel to a line means tangent slope $90$; count roots of $f'(x)=90$.
questions.justification: Routine: reduce to a quartic and count its roots; the quartic factorises or yields to sign changes. Single step, familiar pattern.

questions.key_step: Largest circle about the point has radius = minimum distance, found where the normal passes through the point (or by minimising a quadratic in $x$).
questions.justification: Two-step: identify r as min distance, then optimise with a parametrised point; no options and the arithmetic is mildly heavy. Slightly above a plain optimisation.

questions.key_step: Two conditions at the point: value and slope; solve for $a,b$ with care over $(1+b)$ cancellation.
questions.justification: Routine two-equation system after differentiating a rational function; only algebraic care needed.
questions.nearest_anchor: 2024-P2-Q3 (L1); chained a little longer, so L2

questions.key_step: Simplify $g$ to $\frac{1+e^x}{1-e^x}$, show $g'>0$; increasing implies one-one.
questions.justification: Single simplification and one derivative sign; both statements follow from monotonicity.

questions.key_step: Sign of $f'$ is $-(x-1)(x+1)$: monotonic on $(-\infty,-1)$, $(1,\infty)$ but not on $\mathbb{R}$.
questions.justification: One derivative and a sign scheme; option elimination makes it easy.

questions.key_step: Set $h=f-g$ and integrate $h''=6x$ twice using the boundary data; then test each option.
questions.justification: Chain of several steps plus four statements to check, one with a subtle bound; at Main level but a careful verify-all-options question.

questions.key_step: Factor $f'$ using the given root $x=2$, locate the local maximum, and evaluate with surds.
questions.justification: Routine but evaluation at an irrational point is error-prone; four options help.

questions.key_step: Opposite-sign roots of $f'$ $\iff f'(0)<0$.
questions.justification: One standard condition on the roots of the derivative quadratic; very short.

questions.key_step: Subtract the two derivatives to isolate the common root $x=1$.
questions.justification: One observation (difference of derivatives) and a substitution; standard JEE Main trick.

questions.key_step: Write $S$ in terms of $l_1,l_2$ with $A_1=\left(\frac{l_1}{4}\right)^2$, $A_2=\pi\left(\frac{l_2}{2\pi}\right)^2$, then differentiate.
questions.justification: Standard constrained optimisation; modelling then one derivative.

questions.key_step: Compare derivatives on $[0,3]$ via $1\le1+x^2\le10$; then compare maxima at the right end.
questions.justification: Four statements, each decided by a simple bound; routine care needed.

questions.key_step: Split the modulus at $x=2$, observe $f$ is decreasing on both pieces, take endpoint values.
questions.justification: Piecewise function with a modulus; short once split. Routine for JEE Main.

questions.key_step: Write $AB^2$ as $16\sec^2\theta+9\csc^2\theta$ and complete the square (or use Cauchy-Schwarz).
questions.justification: Standard tangent-intercept minimisation; one identity decides.
questions.nearest_anchor: 2024-P2-Q3 (L1); numerical format adds a little: L2

questions.key_step: Write $f(x)=(x+1)(ax+b)$, use the touching conditions $f(1)=1$, $f'(1)=1$.
questions.justification: Two conditions for a quadratic, then a normal intercept; mild chain at Main level.

questions.key_step: $f'$ increasing makes the sign of $g'$ follow $x-(1-x)$, so $\alpha=\frac{1}{2}$; then the tangent identity for $1,2,3$.
questions.justification: Two short familiar ideas linked (symmetry of g and inverse-tangent sum identity).

questions.key_step: Spot $\frac{d}{dx}(x\ln x\,f)$ in the hypothesis and use monotonicity of $g$.
questions.justification: Needs the product-rule recognition and bound reasoning; the data is flawed, so the reasoning (vacuous truth) is subtle for a student. Level 3.

questions.key_step: Find the four turning points, then use sign evaluations to count all five crossings.
questions.justification: Needs a systematic sign-change count over several intervals; numerical format without options and slip-prone.

questions.key_step: Differentiate, find $x^*=\sqrt{21}$, then compare the integer neighbours $4$ and $5$.
questions.justification: Standard greatest-term technique with one comparison of two fractions.

questions.key_step: Put $t=e^{2x}$ and count positive roots of $t^4-t^3-3t^2-t+1$ (limits give at least two; Descartes gives at most two).
questions.justification: Needs the exponential substitution plus a root-count argument (palindromic or Descartes); no options.

questions.key_step: Volume $V=x(30-2x)^2$; maximise, then compute the surface area of the open box.
questions.justification: Textbook open-box maximisation; one derivative and one substitution.

questions.key_step: Log-differentiate; the critical point is $\sin^2x=\frac{3}{4}$, and the maximum value is $e^{3/8}$.
questions.justification: Logarithmic differentiation of $u^v$, a trigonometric critical equation and exponent arithmetic with a named constant; several stages, options help.

questions.key_step: Factor $f'$ through $\cos x$ to get $x=\frac{\pi}{6},\frac{5\pi}{6}$; decide the maximum by comparing with endpoints.
questions.justification: Multiple-angle algebra in the derivative plus comparison of several candidate values; moderately long.

questions.key_step: $f''>0\Rightarrow f'$ increasing, so $g'>0\iff\frac{x}{3}>3-x$.
questions.justification: One step: monotone $f'$ turns the sign of $g'$ into a linear inequality.
questions.nearest_anchor: 2024-P2-Q3 (L1); fine point about reading g'(x): L2

questions.key_step: Recognise $4x^3-3x=\cos3\theta$ with $x=\cos\theta$; show monotonicity for uniqueness.
questions.justification: Pattern recognition (triple-angle in a cubic) then a derivative; short but the cue must be seen.

questions.key_step: Differentiate; the numerator collapses to $-(x^2+16)$.
questions.justification: One quotient-rule derivative whose numerator has a fixed sign.

questions.key_step: Recognise $f'(\frac{1}{2})=f'(1)=f'(\frac{3}{2})=0$ and apply Rolle to $f'$ twice.
questions.justification: Hidden symmetry plus Rolle's theorem twice; options need careful discrimination between 'exactly one' and 'at least two'.

questions.key_step: Increasing function from $0$ to $e^3$ gives $a=0$, $b=e^3$; then the point-line distance.
questions.justification: Two routine stages (range, distance) with careful exponent algebra.

questions.key_step: Swap $x\leftrightarrow\frac{1}{x}$ and eliminate to get $9x^2f(x)=5x^4-2x^2-4$.
questions.justification: Standard functional-equation elimination followed by a sign scheme for a quartic derivative.

questions.key_step: Count the zeros of $f$ and $f'$ by graphs or Rolle's theorem: $m=3$, $n=2$.
questions.justification: Needs a careful count of intersections of exponential and polynomial/line curves without options; error-prone for students.

questions.key_step: Express the three terms through $d$ using $a_6=2$ and maximise the cubic $P(d)$.
questions.justification: Setup with a known term then a cubic derivative with factorisation; routine.

questions.key_step: Differentiate, note $f'$ is undefined at $0$ and zero at $-1$, and read the sign scheme.
questions.justification: Cusp at the origin must be examined separately; one derivative and a sign scheme.

questions.key_step: Area $=x(54-2x^2)$; one derivative.
questions.justification: Single-variable optimisation of a cubic; textbook.

questions.key_step: Find critical points $-3,-1,2$ and compare with the endpoint values; the endpoints give both $M$ and $m$.
questions.justification: Standard closed-interval extrema; arithmetic with large cubes needs care.

questions.key_step: Differentiate the integral; sign changes only at odd-multiplicity roots; list maxima and minima.
questions.justification: Long factored sign scheme with parity of exponents; mechanical but needs care to avoid the even-multiplicity trap.

questions.key_step: Centre on the axis $(0,6-r)$; tangency to the lines gives $\frac{6-r}{2}=r$.
questions.justification: Geometric modelling with a symmetry assumption, then a single distance equation; the wording (minimum area, 'touching') is ambiguous.

questions.key_step: Recognise $\sqrt{8x-x^2-12}$ as the $y$-coordinate on a semicircle and the expression as $PQ^2$ for $Q(7,4)$.
questions.justification: The key idea (a squared distance to a point on a semicircle) is not routine and the arc restriction must be handled; no options.

questions.key_step: $f''<0$ for statement (II), and a positive lower bound of $f'$ for statement (I).
questions.justification: Two short derivative checks; bounding $f'$ uses the interval's endpoint.

questions.key_step: Logarithmic differentiation: $f'=x^x(1+\ln x)$.
questions.justification: One familiar derivative and one inequality.

questions.key_step: Combine the derivative into one fraction; zeros of the numerator and points where the denominator vanishes (with $f$ defined) are critical.
questions.justification: Fractional power: routine derivative, but the undefined-derivative point must be counted.

questions.key_step: $f'=-(1+\sin x)\le0$: strictly decreasing, so (S2) fails; sign change gives (S1).
questions.justification: Short derivative check plus the intermediate value theorem.

questions.key_step: Recognise $3f'f''+ff'''$ inside $\frac{d}{dx}(f^3f'')$ and apply Rolle's theorem three times.
questions.justification: Hidden product-rule structure, Rolle chain and careful zero counting (with the $f^2$ factor); no options and an unusual idea.

questions.key_step: Rewrite $f$ with $\cos4x$, factor $f'$, and demand $\sin4x=\frac{1}{2(p-4)}$ be impossible.
questions.justification: Trig simplification, factorisation with a parameter and a range argument including the degenerate case; no options.

questions.key_step: Differentiate; the single critical point $x=\frac{19}{5}$ and the endpoints decide the extremes.
questions.justification: Routine closed-interval extrema with radicals.

questions.key_step: Set up the sides $a,b$ with angle $\theta$ and maximise $8+10\sin2\theta$; then evaluate $(a+b)^2$ at $\theta=45^\circ$.
questions.justification: Geometric set-up (the figure) is the main work; then a trig optimisation with a double angle.

questions.key_step: Maximum at $x=\frac{1}{e}$ means $f\left(\frac{1}{e}\right)>f\left(\frac{1}{\pi}\right)$; simplify to $e^\pi>\pi^e$.
questions.justification: The idea (compare with the maximum) is standard; algebra to rewrite exponents.

questions.key_step: Factor $f'=-6\sin x\cos x(2\cos x+\sqrt3)$ and read the sign scheme on $(0,2\pi)$.
questions.justification: Factorised trigonometric derivative and a five-point sign scheme.

questions.key_step: Factor $f'=6(x-a)(x-2a)$, so $\alpha=a$ and $\alpha^2=2a$ give $a=2$.
questions.justification: Direct factorisation and one condition; short.

questions.key_step: Line through $(3,5)$ with intercepts $p,q$: AM-GM on $\frac{3}{p}+\frac{5}{q}=1$ gives $pq\ge60$ (area $30$).
questions.justification: Known lemma (midpoint property) or AM-GM; short.

questions.key_step: Corner $(x,y)$ on the parabola: area $(24-x)2y=48y-y^3$; maximise.
questions.justification: Standard inscribed-rectangle optimisation in one variable.

questions.key_step: Find the local minimum $x=-\frac{\lambda}{\sqrt3}$; solve the rational inequality to get $(-3,-2)$; translate to $\lambda$.
questions.justification: Four routine stages (critical point, type, inequality, interval) with a parameter.
